sections.body:
A **family** is a group of people who belong to each other. They may live in the same house, or they may not.

Every child has a family. Some families are big. Some are small. Some have a lot of people in them, and some have only two.

There are words for the people in a family. You probably know some of them already. You say **mum** or **mom**, you say **dad**. You say **brother**, **sister**, **grandma**, **grandpa**.

Every family has its own names. Some children call their grandmother *bà ngoại*. Some call her *grandma*. Some call their grandmother *Nana*. The name is not the important part. The person is.

Talking about your family is easy once you have the words. You can say *This is my mum.* You can say *My dad is a cook.* You can say *I have one sister and no brothers.*

And when you meet somebody new, you can introduce your family, the way you would introduce a friend.

In this book you will learn the family words, the way to say a sentence about each person, and how to be kind about families that look different from yours.
examples: This is my mum. Her name is Hoa.
I have one sister. Her name is Lan.
sections.heading: Your family is the people who belong with you

sections.body:
Talking about a family is easy when you keep it to one idea at a time.

Start with the name. *This is my brother, Bao.*

Then say one thing about them. *He is six.* Or *He likes football.* Or *She has long hair.*

Then say one thing about what they do. *My mum is a nurse.* *My dad drives a bus.* *My grandma grows vegetables in the garden.*

You can also say how you feel about somebody. *I love my grandma.* *My brother is my best friend.*

A small word helps a lot: **my**. *My mum, my dad, my aunt.* It tells the listener that the person belongs to you. It sounds warm.

And **we** is useful for the family as a whole. *We live in Hanoi.* *We go to the park on Sunday.*

Try to keep each sentence short. A short sentence is easy to say and easy to understand. That is all a good sentence needs to be.
examples: My mum is a nurse. She works at a hospital.
My sister is six. She likes painting.
We live near my school. We walk there.
sections.heading: Saying one thing about each person

sections.body:
These are the words for the people in your family. Here is what each one means.

Mum is your mother. **Dad** is your father. Some children use *mom* and *dad*, and some use *mommy* and *daddy*. All of them mean the same thing.

Brother is a boy or man with the same parents as you. **Sister** is a girl or woman with the same parents as you. If the child is older than you, the word *older* fits: *my older brother*.

Grandmother is your mum's mother, or your dad's mother. **Grandfather** is your mum's father, or your dad's father. You might call them *grandma* and *grandpa*.

Aunt is the wife of your uncle, or your mum's sister. **Uncle** is the husband of your aunt, or your dad's brother. Sometimes these words are used for a friend of the family too, and that is fine.

Cousin is a child of your aunt or uncle. Cousins are like brothers and sisters, but they do not have the same parents as you.

Nephew and **niece** are the words for the children of your brother or sister.

And **parents** is the word for your mum and your dad together.
examples: My aunt visits us in the summer.
sections.heading: The family words, one by one

terms.example: My mum is a nurse. She works at a hospital.
terms.gloss: The word for your mother. Some families say mom or mommy instead.

terms.example: My grandmother grows vegetables in the garden.
terms.gloss: Your mum's mother or your dad's mother. You often call her grandma.

terms.example: My aunt lives in Da Nang.
terms.gloss: Your mum's sister, or the wife of your uncle. Sometimes a family friend is called an aunt too.

terms.example: My cousin Mai is my age. We play together every weekend.
terms.gloss: A child of your aunt or your uncle. A cousin is like a brother or sister, but not a real one.

terms.example: My parents work at the weekend too.
terms.gloss: The word for your mum and your dad together.

sections.body:
When a visitor comes to your house, or you meet somebody new, you can introduce your family. It is a nice thing to do.

First, greet the visitor. *Hello, Aunt Mai. Welcome.*

Next, stand near the person you are talking about.

Then point, or look at them, and say who they are. *This is my mum.*

After that, say one small thing about them. *She is a teacher.*

Then let the visitor talk. Do not keep talking for everybody. A good introduction gives the conversation to the other person.

And when the visitor leaves, say goodbye to them and to your family. *Goodbye, Aunt Mai. See you soon.*

Introductions work in a team, too. If you are with your sister, you can share it. *This is my sister. Her name is Lan. Lan, this is Aunt Mai.*
examples: Hello, Uncle Bao. Welcome to our house.
This is my grandma. She is called Nana.
Lan, this is Aunt Mai. Aunt Mai, this is Lan.
sections.heading: How to introduce your family to somebody
steps: Greet the visitor and welcome them.
Stand near the person you are talking about.
Say one small thing about them.
Let the visitor talk for a while.
Say goodbye when the visit ends.

sections.body:
There is no single shape for a family.

Some children live with both parents. Some live with one parent. Some live with their grandparents. Some have two mums or two dads. Some have a big family, some a small one.

All of these are families. A family is about who loves you, not about a rule.

This matters because children sometimes tell each other what a family should look like. If somebody says *your family is not right*, you can answer simply: *This is my family, and I like it.*

You can also ask about somebody else's family without making fun. *How many people are in your family?* is a good question. *Who do you live with?* is also good.

And listen to the answer. Some families are big and loud. Some are small and quiet. Both are fine.

Do not tell anybody else a secret from a family. If somebody says something private to you, keep it. That is what a good family member does.
examples: I live with my mum and my grandma.
How many people are in your family?
This is my family, and I like it.
sections.heading: Every family is different

sections.body:
Sometimes people ask you questions about your family. It is fine to answer. It is also fine to say only what you want to say.

If you do not want to answer, say it simply and politely. *I do not want to talk about that right now.* Then change the subject or walk away.

If somebody asks about a person who is not there, or about something that feels private, go and tell a grown-up you trust. That is not being rude. It is being careful.

And if a friend says something unkind about your family, do not answer with something unkind back. Say *I do not like that*, and go and tell a teacher or a grown-up.

Your family is yours. You get to say how much you share, and with whom.
examples: I would rather not talk about that now.
Please do not ask me about that.
I do not like that. Please stop.
sections.heading: When you are asked about your family

item.summary: Your family is the people who belong with you. After reading this you can name the people in your family, say what each of them does, and introduce your family to somebody new.
item.title: Talking About Your Family
